name: Halo pairs 300 km apart: 20->8 ms field, then no field (Burke 2013)
origin: Persinger lab, Laurentian University (Burke, Gauthier, Rouleau & Persinger 2013), Arduino-driven toroid ('halo')
summary: Burke, Gauthier, Rouleau & Persinger 2013: in two pairs 300 km apart, each person wearing a ring coil ('halo') above the ears, the stimulus partner received six 30-s sound and light trains first with a shared rotating field, then without it (230 points, delays shortening from 20 to 8 ms in 2-ms steps). Persinger's lab reported sLORETA changes in the distant response partners only with the field and only for the sounds.
notes: Verified from the paper: 4 people (stimulus partners in Timmins, response partners in Sudbury, Ontario); 3 audio (6, 8, 15 Hz) and 3 light (7, 10, 40 Hz) trains from an iPhone 4, 30 s on and 30 s off, the no-field sequence using the same six in another order; the response partners' 19-channel QEEG recorded throughout by investigators not told which stimulus was playing; each halo 225 turns of 16-gauge wire on a 25.4-cm ring "just above the dorsal ear", driven by an Arduino Uno with "230 amplitude-modulated points (333 Hz, 1.45 Hz cycle)", about 1 uT, "phase modulated in 2 ms increments (20 ms delay to 8 ms delay) such that an increase in angular velocity occurred"; field and no-field order counterbalanced across the two pairs (persinger-burke-2013-halo runs the other order). This helmet has no toroid: its eight coils point into the head, while a toroid's field runs around the ring, so the field geometry is not reproduced. How the Arduino combined the 230 points with the delays is not described; here the seven delays (20, 18 ... 8 ms) become the time on each coil of a counter-clockwise ring rotation, as in the lab's 8-solenoid rings, whose "angular velocity" language the paper keeps; with seven delays on eight coils, the 20-ms step falls one coil earlier on each pass (Fp1, then Fp2, then FT8 ...). The 230 point values were never published; the built-in accelerating burst stands in, 230 points of 3 ms repeated back to back (690 ms, 1.45 Hz). Ring sites Fp1, FT7, TP7, O1, O2, TP8, FT8, Fp2. Both partners' helmets run this program; the lab kept time by cell phone and synchronised stopwatches. Light flashes can trigger seizures in susceptible people. n = 4; many sLORETA voxel and band comparisons reported at p < 0.001 with no correction described; later papers give the distance as 400 km; published in JCER; never independently replicated. Independent double-blind tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012). Do not use results for decisions about real people. Nobody with epilepsy, a seizure history or photosensitivity should take part in either role.
setting: Stimulus partner: seated, helmet on, receiving the six 30-s trains (sound at 6, 8 and 15 Hz, light at 7, 10 and 40 Hz), one per minute from the start of each phase, in a different order in the two phases. Response partner: elsewhere, second helmet running this program, EEG recorded throughout by someone who does not know which train is playing or which phase has the field.
schedule: One session per pair; run half of the pairs with persinger-burke-2013-halo.
source: Burke, Gauthier, Rouleau & Persinger 2013, Experimental demonstration of potential entanglement of brain activity over 300 km ..., J Conscious Explor Res 4(1):35-44 https://jcer.com/index.php/jcj/article/view/279 ; Rouleau & Persinger 2015, J Electromagn Anal Appl 7(2) (later description of the toroid protocol, 400 km) https://file.scirp.org/Html/1-9801584_54135.htm ; Scott et al. 2015, J Conscious Explor Res 6(9):658-684 (toroid build: 225 turns on a 25.4-cm ring) https://jcer.com/index.php/jcj/article/view/493 ; Dotta & Persinger 2012, "Doubling" of local photon emissions when two simultaneous, spatially-separated, chemiluminescent reactions share the same magnetic field configurations, J Biophys Chem 3:72-80 (859- and 230-point patterns at 1 ms; primer/effector order) https://file.scirp.org/Html/17181.html ; Juden-Kelly, Dotta, Vares & Persinger 2015, JCER 6(9):728-737 (Burst-X: 230 points) https://jcer.com/index.php/jcj/article/view/497 ; Carniello 2020, PhD thesis, Laurentian University (230-point burst-firing file) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/items/8c92763c-cd19-4a21-b242-3b572a28ce55 ; Persinger & Lavallee 2010, Theoretical and experimental evidence of macroscopic entanglement between human brain activity and photon emissions, J Conscious Explor Res 1(7):785-807 (20+2 notation; coil 1 left frontal, coil 8 right prefrontal) https://jcer.com/index.php/jcj/article/view/99 ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1-6 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/

phases.name: Field: 230 pts x 3 ms, delay 20->8 ms per coil, CCW
No field: six stimulus trains to the partner
